items.headline: U.S. Markets Closed for Weekend After Tech-Led Sell-Off on Friday
items.summary: U.S. equity markets are closed today, Saturday, October 17, 2026. The last trading session on Friday, October 16, 2026, saw major indices close lower, driven by a broad sell-off in technology stocks and increasing concerns over the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout. Both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite recorded their worst weekly performance since June.

items.headline: TechNova Inc. surged on AI chip breakthrough
items.summary: Shares of TechNova Inc. climbed 12% following the announcement of a breakthrough AI chip designed to revolutionize data center efficiency.

items.headline: GreenEnergy Corp. rises on multi-billion dollar contract
items.summary: GreenEnergy Corp. saw an 8.5% increase after securing a multi-billion-dollar contract to supply renewable energy infrastructure across Europe.

items.headline: HealthPlus Pharma jumps on positive drug trial results
items.summary: HealthPlus Pharma experienced a 7% jump as its latest drug trial results for a rare autoimmune disease exceeded expectations.

items.headline: MDXHEALTH plunges after suspending guidance
items.summary: MDXHEALTH ($MDXH) shares plunged 68.01% after the company announced preliminary Q3 2026 revenue and suspended its full-year 2026 revenue guidance.

items.headline: Fractyl Health Inc. tumbles
items.summary: FRACTYL HEALTH INC ($GUTS) tumbled 59.13% in Friday's trading session.

items.headline: Micron Technology falls amid AI worries
items.summary: Micron Technology ($MU) fell 5.6% as worries deepened about the longevity of the AI buildout frenzy.

items.headline: Intel drops on tech sector weakness
items.summary: Intel ($INTC) lost 5.8% as big tech companies continued to weigh on the overall market.

items.headline: Tech Sector Experiences Weekly Decline, Defensive Stocks See Inflows
items.summary: The Information Technology sector was the biggest drag on Friday, falling 0.9% and marking a 3.9% decline for the week, as investors rotated out of semiconductor and AI-linked shares. Conversely, defensive sectors such as Materials (+1.6%) and Financials (+1.1%) saw gains. Healthcare, consumer staples, and financials generally outperformed.

items.headline: Inflation Concerns Persist as PPI Rises and Trade Deficit Widens
items.summary: September's Producer Price Index (PPI) jumped 1.3%, the largest monthly gain since March 2022, primarily driven by energy prices. Headline CPI inflation also rose higher than expected to 3.7% annually. Additionally, the U.S. goods and services deficit widened to $105.6 billion in August, with import prices increasing 1.1% and export prices rising 2.2% in September.

items.headline: Federal Deficit Nears $2 Trillion; Fed Signals October Pause
items.summary: The federal budget deficit reached nearly $2 trillion for the past fiscal year, the largest since 2021. Despite rising inflation, market expectations largely indicate the Federal Reserve is likely to keep interest rates unchanged this month.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season Mixed with Strong Beat Rate, Lower Magnitude
items.summary: Approximately 9% of S&P 500 companies have reported Q3 earnings, with 84% beating EPS estimates, above the 5-year average. However, the magnitude of these beats is lower than average, at 2.6% above estimates. The blended earnings growth rate for Q3 is currently 29.0%. Major companies like Meta ($META) and Tesla ($TSLA) are scheduled to report next week.
